name: Non-text Content
remarks: Images, icons and the web-page report's figures have text alternatives that axe and tests confirm. The simulation canvas has a generated text description and each plotted series is available as a table in the export dialog and the web-page report. A curve's shape is not narrated, and a description is not equivalent to watching the simulation. The instructor PDFs carry no alternative text.

name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
remarks: The application plays no prerecorded audio or video. It synthesizes sound only on request (the gravitational-wave audio and the sonification), each with a text equivalent.

name: Captions (Prerecorded)
remarks: The application plays no prerecorded audio or video. It synthesizes sound only on request (the gravitational-wave audio and the sonification), each with a text equivalent.

name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
remarks: The application plays no prerecorded audio or video. It synthesizes sound only on request (the gravitational-wave audio and the sonification), each with a text equivalent.

name: Captions (Live)
remarks: The application streams no live media and plays no prerecorded video.

name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
remarks: The application streams no live media and plays no prerecorded video.

name: Info and Relationships
remarks: Pages use landmarks, ordered headings, real lists and tables with header cells, and the scripted manual checks confirm landmark and heading order on the surfaces they open. Since Prompt 279 every page of the walk inventory has a recorded outline (one h1, no skipped level, one main, every navigation and region named) that a test holds it to in both languages. axe judges only the relationships it can detect. The instructor PDFs are untagged, so they declare no structure; the student reports are tagged but unvalidated.

name: Meaningful Sequence
remarks: Focus and reading order on the surfaces the manual spec opens follow the visual order. No method judges the reading order of every page. The PDFs are read in the order the text was drawn, which is the intended order but is not declared.

name: Sensory Characteristics
remarks: No method here judges whether an instruction depends on shape, position or color alone. Investigation text that points at the simulation was not reviewed against this criterion.

name: Orientation
remarks: No test rotates the display. Nothing in the markup locks an orientation, but that is an absence of evidence, not an evaluation.

name: Identify Input Purpose
remarks: The few fields that collect personal information (a student's name for a report) are checked by axe's autocomplete rule where it applies. No method evaluates every field.

name: Use of Color
remarks: Links in text are distinguishable without color, and the reports print what kind a number is as a word beside it. Colors in the simulation canvas that distinguish bodies were not evaluated against this criterion. Under forced colors a pressed, selected or current button, link or tab keeps a mark that is not a color (tests assert it on every page of the walk inventory).

name: Audio Control
remarks: Sound starts only when the reader asks for it and stops on the same control. The audio and sonification specs cover those two features, not every control that can make sound.

name: Contrast (Minimum)
remarks: axe measures text contrast on every listed surface, in both languages and in all four themes on the shell pages, with no rule disabled. It reports as incomplete, and cannot judge, text over the canvas, images and gradients; the canvas labels are measured by a separate harness (e2e/canvasLegibility.spec.js) for the scenes it covers. The design ratchet holds the text tokens, the accent, the status colors and a label on its button's face to 4.5:1 on every surface of each of the four themes, and records the ratios so they only rise; it found and fixed three pairs (Deep's muted text, Daylight's accent and warning).

name: Resize Text
remarks: Pages reflow at 200% and 400% zoom (e2e/accessibilityManual.spec.js) and the viewport tag never forbids page zoom. Text resize alone, in a browser that scales only text, was not tested.

name: Images of Text
remarks: No method looks for text drawn as an image. Canvas labels are drawn text by necessity; the wordmark and figures were not reviewed.

name: Reflow
remarks: The scripted check loads the listed surfaces at 320 and 640 CSS pixels and asserts no horizontal scrolling for content other than the canvas, tables with their own scroll region and the instructor documents. Since Prompt 279 every page of the walk inventory but the original-version page is loaded at 320 px in both languages, the Observatory with an observation open and a lesson open beside the sandbox as well, and nothing may lie beyond the viewport outside a scroll container of the page's own; it found and fixed two. 400% zoom is the 320 px width, not a browser's zoom, and text spacing was not tested.

name: Non-text Contrast
remarks: Control and focus-indicator contrast is checked where axe can reach it (its color-contrast rule covers text, not the borders and icons this criterion names). The design ratchet holds the focus ring's color and the object hues on the sky to 3:1 in all four themes. A control's border is not held to 3:1, and the drawn bodies and plot marks were not measured against the criterion. Under forced colors every control keeps an edge and a plot keeps its own palette.

name: Text Spacing
remarks: No test applies the text-spacing overrides. Fixed-height containers that could clip were not audited.

name: Content on Hover or Focus
remarks: No method here exercises content that appears on hover or focus, such as tooltips and the object inspector's help.

name: Keyboard
remarks: Every control a pointer can press on a page of the walk inventory, in the state the page opens in, is reached by Tab, and each page's primary control answers its key (e2e/a11ySweep.spec.js, both languages). Placement has a keyboard form; the sandbox's zoom and pan, the 3-D lab's and the spacetime view's cameras, the observer's angle, a window's position and size and a run of rows in the Observatory each have a control the keyboard operates. Panels and dialogs a page opens later are covered where a named spec opens them, not everywhere. Dragging to feel a throw has no keyboard equivalent, by design; the typed form gives the number instead.

name: No Keyboard Trap
remarks: Every modal opens through one module that traps focus within it, restores focus on close and answers Escape (tests/dialogInventory.test.js fails on one that does not). The walk Tabs once round every page of the walk inventory and finds no trap; it found that a dialog ending in a disclosure never gave the disclosure focus, which is fixed. The figure builder's embedded frame gives focus back. Third-party frames were not tested.

name: Character Key Shortcuts
remarks: Single-key shortcuts are ignored while a text field has focus, except Escape. Whether a reader can turn them off or remap them was not evaluated, and the criterion requires it where a shortcut is a single printable character.

name: Timing Adjustable
remarks: No investigation or report has a time limit. The simulation runs in real time by design, and the reader can pause it. Timed toasts and the start-up failsafe were not evaluated for adjustment.

name: Pause, Stop, Hide
remarks: Decorative animation stops with prefers-reduced-motion and the simulation can be paused from the transport bar or the space bar. The orbital motion itself does not stop for the media query because it is the content. Every keyframes and scheduler in the sources is in tools/motion-inventory.json, and no page has a running animation or transition with reduced motion; four families of lesson instruments now start still under it. Six instruments (the resonance and exoplanet ones) start by themselves with no pause control, and the reader's own Motion setting reaches only the application page.

name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
remarks: No method measures flash frequency or area. No feature is designed to flash; the starfield and the gravitational-wave views were not measured.

name: Bypass Blocks
remarks: The skip link is the first tab stop on the simulation page and goes to the main region (e2e/accessibilityManual.spec.js). Other pages were not tested for a skip mechanism; the shared shell's navigation is a short list of groups.

name: Page Titled
remarks: Every stamped page has a title that follows the page language, and the PDFs carry a document title. The generated web-page report has a title naming the investigation and the student.

name: Focus Order
remarks: Focus order, traps and restoration are asserted on the surfaces the manual spec lists. The walk makes one full round of every page of the walk inventory and shows that the round is complete and returns; whether the order is the meaningful one is judged only where the manual spec asserts it. One test for each focus pattern (a dialog, a lesson's opening and its step change, an observation opening, a disclosure, a rail panel) shows focus going somewhere that exists and being given back.

name: Link Purpose (In Context)
remarks: axe confirms every link has an accessible name on the surfaces it runs. Whether each name states a purpose in context was not reviewed.

name: Multiple Ways
remarks: The shared navigation, the Library and the investigations browser reach investigations in more than one way. No test confirms that every page is reachable in more than one.

name: Headings and Labels
remarks: Headings are ordered and non-empty and controls are labeled on the evaluated surfaces. Whether each describes its content was not reviewed.

name: Focus Visible
remarks: Keyboard focus is visible on the controls the manual specs exercise. Not every control state was captured. Under forced colors the first six Tab stops of three pages draw a focus ring (Prompt 279).

name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
remarks: Dialogs isolate the page behind them and the sticky shell was checked on the surfaces opened. The walk asserts that every Tab stop of every page of the walk inventory has its box inside the viewport while it has focus. It does not test whether another element lies over that box.

name: Pointer Gestures
remarks: Pinch zooms the canvas and drag pans or aims. Since Prompt 278 the sandbox's view pad pans and zooms with single presses, as do the pads of the 3-D lab and the spacetime view; the rail's controls and the keyboard give the alternatives for placement. The throw-velocity drag has none by design.

name: Pointer Cancellation
remarks: No method evaluates down-event versus up-event activation across controls.

name: Label in Name
remarks: axe's label-content-name-mismatch rule runs on the listed surfaces (it is an experimental rule that reports little). Not otherwise reviewed.

name: Motion Actuation
remarks: No function is triggered by device motion or user motion.

name: Dragging Movements
remarks: Every drag the interaction contract registers has an alternative that needs one pointer and no path, each walked in e2e/a11ySweep.spec.js or the spec the contract names: placing a body and its velocity (a typed form that reaches the same state, e2e/accessibilityParity.spec.js), panning and zooming the sandbox, orbiting the 3-D lab and the spacetime view, the observer's angle, moving and sizing a window, and selecting rows, a run of rows and pixels in the Observatory. Dragging a throw to feel its speed has no non-dragging equivalent beyond the number.

name: Target Size (Minimum)
remarks: Controls are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, and 44 on a coarse pointer, as measured on the phone and tablet projects. Every checkbox and radio on every page of the walk inventory, and in the lesson panel and the settings dialog, is 24 px or more (the 13 px boxes recorded as Z-1 are gone). The footer attribution links in running text are smaller and rely on the inline exception.

name: Language of Page
remarks: Every stamped page and generated document states its language and follows the reader's choice. axe checks the listed surfaces in both languages; the shell check covers every stamped page. The Spanish text is a project translation that no outside reader has reviewed.

name: Language of Parts
remarks: Bilingual pages mark the Spanish text with lang. Quotations, names and code in the other language inside a sentence were not audited.

name: On Focus
remarks: No evaluated control changes context when focused. Not every control was exercised.

name: On Input
remarks: The language and theme switches are explicit controls and change nothing until chosen. No other input's behavior was evaluated.

name: Consistent Navigation
remarks: The shared shell stamps the same navigation in the same order on its pages. The simulation page has its own control rail.

name: Consistent Identification
remarks: No method compares the names of repeated controls across pages.

name: Consistent Help
remarks: The application offers no help mechanism repeated across pages beyond the navigation itself; there is no chat, contact form or phone number.

name: Error Identification
remarks: Errors are attached to the field they are about in precise placement and the system builder (e2e/accessibilityParity.spec.js, e2e/systemBuilder.spec.js), and the report asks for a name before it builds. Other tools' fields were not evaluated.

name: Labels or Instructions
remarks: Fields carry visible labels with their units named. Instructions for the authoring tools were not reviewed.

name: Error Suggestion
remarks: Numeric fields and answer checks say what was expected. Not every error message suggests a fix.

name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
remarks: The application makes no legal commitment and takes no financial transaction. A student's saved work can be exported and nothing leaves the browser without an explicit action.

name: Redundant Entry
remarks: A student's name is remembered for reports and submissions in the same session; saved progress is restored. Other tools were not evaluated.

name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
remarks: There is no authentication, account or password. The instructor passphrase is a decryption key for downloaded materials, not a sign-in.

name: Parsing (obsolete in WCAG 2.2)
remarks: Removed from WCAG 2.2; for 2.1 the parsing rules are met by HTML that parses without error, which the page tests and axe's duplicate-id rules confirm on the listed surfaces.

name: Name, Role, Value
remarks: axe finds no violation of its name, role and value rules on the listed surfaces. It does not evaluate custom widgets' keyboard behavior; the manual specs cover the dialogs, the rail and the lesson controls.

name: Status Messages
remarks: Status changes are announced through the polite live region #srStatus on the simulation page, and the manual specs assert announcements where they check a feature. The sandbox's zoom, the 3-D lab's camera, a window move and an armed run of rows are each said once, when the pressing stops, in both languages (e2e/a11ySweep.spec.js). Not every message in every tool was verified, and none with a screen reader.
